label: START F6
title: Probiotic with antibiotics to prevent C. difficile diarrhoea
statement: Probiotics used with antibiotics in patients who are not immunocompromised or severely debilitated for the prevention of Clostridioides difficile -associated diarrhoea.

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: A probiotic taken during an antibiotic course may lower the chance of a serious bowel infection called C. difficile diarrhoea, in people whose immune system is working normally.

medicine_groups.name: Probiotics (medicines that meet this criterion)
medicine_groups.note: Most probiotics are sold without a prescription, so a record may show few of them. A product counts when its ingredients are lactobacillus, bifidobacterium or saccharomyces.

medicine_groups.name: Antibiotics by mouth (the medicines whose supply raises the check)
medicine_groups.note: Each course counts on its own. Skin creams, eye drops and ear drops do not count. Nexium Hp7 is a Helicobacter pylori pack that contains two antibiotics, and it counts as a course. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

medicine_groups.name: Medicines that suppress the immune system (these remove the finding)
medicine_groups.note: Their supply suggests the person may be immunocompromised, so the criterion does not apply. This list is short and is not complete. Chemotherapy and long courses of high-dose steroids also suppress the immune system.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group B antibiotic is supplied and no Group A probiotic has a supply date within 7 days of that antibiotic supply. Do not suspect a finding when the record shows a Group C medicine, or a line that records the person as immunocompromised, on cancer treatment or severely debilitated. Treat each antibiotic course on its own.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the person is immunocompromised or severely debilitated when no line says so, and whether a probiotic was bought over the counter, which is common. Also past C. difficile infection, which makes the check more important, and antibiotics given by a hospital.
ask_the_gp: Whether a probiotic should be suggested during antibiotic courses for this person, if the person's immune system is normal.
